product.name: Aphrodite
product.oneLiner: Name an occasion, upload one selfie, and an AI beauty companion returns a skincare countdown, an outfit rendered on your own body, and a shoppable look board.
product.pitch: Aphrodite is an occasion concierge. You tell it the event and the date and give it one selfie; an LLM orchestrates the YouCam Skin and Apparel VTO APIs as tools, reads your skin and colour, plans a skincare countdown that fits the time you actually have, renders a garment on your own body, and assembles one shoppable look board. Two engines share one event stream — an agentic one and a rule-based fallback — so the product works with no LLM key at all.
product.audience: Someone with a dated event and no confident plan for it: a wedding, a job interview, a first date.
product.antiPattern: A filter app or a skin-scoring gimmick. The product is the plan for a specific day; the renders are its evidence.

rubric._weights: The rules page states the four criteria are EQUALLY WEIGHTED (verified 2026-08-10 at https://youcam-api.devpost.com/rules). An earlier note here said no weights were published — that was wrong. Every criterion therefore carries weight 1 on a 10-point scale; total 50. No finer-grained weighting is published.

criteria.name: Technological Implementation

anchors.9_10: Several YouCam APIs chained so each one's output feeds the next; failures degrade honestly; the integration is provable from the running product, not only from the code.
anchors.5_6: One or two APIs called correctly and in isolation.
anchors.1_3: An API is called once and its result decorates a static page.

criteria.verbatim: How thoroughly and skillfully does the project integrate at least one YouCam API from the Skin/Fashion category? Does the project demonstrate clear consumer or retail value? Does the code reflect genuine effort and a working, non-trivial implementation?

criteria.name: Design

anchors.9_10: Reads as a finished product: one clear path, coherent typography and colour, real empty and error states, works at 320px and at 200% text zoom, keyboard reachable.
anchors.5_6: Attractive on the happy path, thin at the edges.
anchors.1_3: A form and a results dump.

criteria.verbatim: Does the project deliver a complete, coherent product experience — not just a technical proof of concept?

criteria.name: Potential Impact

anchors.9_10: A named audience with a dated need, and a credible commercial story — priced basket, return-confidence, a first-party signal a retailer would want.
anchors.5_6: A plausible audience asserted but not evidenced.
anchors.1_3: A demo looking for a problem.

criteria.verbatim: Does the project make a credible, specific case for solving a real problem for a real audience — and does the solution actually address that problem based on what's demonstrated?

criteria.name: Quality of the Idea

anchors.9_10: Non-obvious API use that only makes sense once you understand the problem; the LLM does planning the APIs cannot do alone.
anchors.5_6: A sensible but expected use of the APIs.
anchors.1_3: The API demo with a new colour scheme.

criteria.verbatim: Is this a creative, non-obvious use of at least one Perfect Corp. YouCam API from the Skin or Fashion category — and does the team demonstrate genuine understanding of the problem space they're working in?

criteria.name: Special category — Skin AI and Apparel VTO as one experience

anchors.9_10: The skin reading visibly determines the garment and the countdown, and the judge sees that chain happen on screen in one run.
anchors.5_6: Both capabilities are present on one page but do not visibly inform each other.
anchors.1_3: Two separate features behind two separate buttons.

Rather than invent personas, the one real entity is modelled as one lens per PUBLISHED criterion, with each lens's wins/loses derived from that criterion's verbatim wording. killGate: fits the combined track: uses both a Skin API and the Apparel VTO API in one run

integrityRisks: The wardrobe is 9 feminine cuts to 1 masculine and 1 neutral, so any 'no preference' default resolves feminine in practice. Until the catalog is widened, the UI must keep ASKING for the cut rather than defaulting — a default here is a guess about the person, and on 2026-08-09 it was rendering the bundled masculine sample in an evening gown with earrings and heels in the basket.
Passing a captured fixture render off as a live YouCam render. Mitigated by a demo flag on the mode event that makes the UI and the print footer say 'demo mode · sample renders · 0 API units'.
Claiming a colour or formality match the wardrobe cannot actually satisfy — a 'tone shift' announced when the catalogue has nothing in that direction.
Skin scores read as medical or worth-based judgements. Scores are health-framed, no-shame wording, and the lowest score is a 'priority area', not a defect.

A judge access code leaked into this public repository: the review-003 panel quoted it in hackathon/reviews/003-*, committed 2026-08-14 and readable on raw.githubusercontent.com. Found 2026-08-16 while checking that the code had NOT reached the public Devpost page. Both codes and APHRODITE_AUTH_SECRET were rotated on the host the same hour, which also invalidated every cookie minted with the leaked code; the old code now returns /unlock?error=1, verified. The files are redacted, but git history still contains the dead string. Cause: the code was passed to the judging panel as liveAccess and the agents echoed it into their findings. Rule that follows: anything handed to a subagent can end up in its report, so a secret must never be part of a prompt whose output gets committed.

demo.accessNotes: Open to everyone: the full flow runs for any visitor at ZERO YouCam units and with no LLM call, and both the announcement bar and the provenance ledger say the renders are captured samples. Two schranken guard the paths that spend: a role code (APHRODITE_LIVE_CODES + APHRODITE_AUTH_SECRET, exchanged at /unlock for a 12h HttpOnly cookie) opens live YouCam and the LLM engine, and a ledger caps live runs at APHRODITE_LIVE_RUN_BUDGET. The codes are NOT in this repo — a public repo carrying them would be no gate at all.
demo.cantFailFallback: YOUCAM_FIXTURES=1 serves captured fixtures for skin, colour, apparel and lighting, so every demo path completes with zero API units even if the YouCam key is dead or rate-limited.
demo._spendCapNote: Hard cap confirmed set on the OpenAI dashboard by the operator, 2026-08-09.

knownGaps.title: Menswear catalog gap
knownGaps.detail: One masculine garment exists (slate-suit, formal, flatters cool). A masculine-presenting shopper has no smart or casual option and no warm-undertone option, so the app correctly declines to claim a colour match for the warm wedding sample. Widening this needs verified front-facing reference imagery, and the render quality of any new reference cannot be confirmed without spending YouCam units.
knownGaps.blockedOn: verified imagery + one units-on capture session

knownGaps.title: The bundled wedding selfie cannot be analysed live
knownGaps.detail: public/samples/selfie.jpg — the selfie the flagship 'Wedding · full-body' preset sends, and the first thing a judge clicks — was rejected by BOTH analysis APIs on 2026-08-10: skin analysis returned error_src_face_too_small and skin-tone returned error_face_angle_downward. Receipts in hackathon/receipts/001/. Fixtures hide this completely, so the demo looks perfect while the same click with units on returns nothing. The colour API succeeds on samples/full-body.jpg, so the API is fine and the sample photo is not. Consequence: closing kill-gate 2 needs a suitable sample image, not just approval to spend.
knownGaps.blockedOn: a sample photo with a larger, frontal face, then one more units-on run

knownGaps.title: Demo video recorded but not uploaded
knownGaps.detail: submission/aphrodite-demo-2026-08-12-voiced.mp4, 88.4 s, 1280x800, cut 2026-08-12 from a production build in demo mode at zero units. SPOKEN narration (local Piper en_US-hfc_female-medium) with burned captions carrying the same words, so what is heard and what is read cannot drift. Every beat records only the state its line describes - the run is driven before recording starts, because a beat is trimmed to the length of its narration and the first cut therefore showed a form filling in while the voice described a render further down the page. Reproducible: scripts/record-demo.mjs then scripts/build-demo-video.mjs, with the lines in submission/narration.txt; swapping VOICE_MODEL re-voices the whole reel. The captions-only cut of 2026-08-10 and the two cuts under submission/archive-old-cuts/ must not be published.
knownGaps.blockedOn: operator: upload to YouTube or Vimeo, paste the URL here and into Devpost

knownGaps.title: What the live API accepts as a face is not what its error strings imply
knownGaps.detail: Five images screened against skin-tone-analysis 2026-08-10. Only samples/full-body.jpg passed - the image with the SMALLEST face. A tight frontal headshot was rejected error_face_angle_downward, a three-quarter portrait error_face_not_forward_facing, and a frontal eye-level headshot error_face_position_too_small at both 900x900 and 2000x2500 with margin. The API is deterministic per image, but 'bigger and more frontal' is demonstrably not the criterion, so choosing a sample that satisfies both analysis endpoints costs one unit per attempt.
knownGaps.blockedOn: trial and error against the live API, budgeted in units

knownGaps.title: The receipts folder does not account for every live task the docs cite
knownGaps.detail: CLAIM_PROOF_MAP.md states 'seven tasks, ~7 units ... all seven are committed', and the two receipt files carry exactly seven. But the same file cites live results with no committed receipt: a SUCCESSFUL skin-analysis run on samples/selfie-2.jpg (the captured cool scores and the committed mask), that photo's error_face_not_forward_facing skin-tone rejection, and two headshot screenings at 900x900 and 2000x2500. That is at least four further tasks. Either the seven-task total understates the real spend - which also makes the ~577 remaining-balance arithmetic wrong - or those runs happened outside the receipt harness and were never recorded. The receipts README's claim that nothing was quietly dropped is in tension with either reading. Found 2026-08-12 by transcribing the receipts into lib/youcam/contract.ts and finding cited results with no task_id behind them.
knownGaps.blockedOn: operator: reconcile the spend against the Perfect Corp console, then correct whichever number is wrong. Not to be resolved by deleting the citations.

closedGaps.title: The kill gate cited an endpoint that 404'd in production
closedGaps.how: /api/dev/verify no longer keys off NODE_ENV. It has two modes split by what they COST: the default replays the request/response contract pinned from the committed receipts and spends zero units, and ?spend=1 makes real calls metered by the same ledger as the product. Both sit behind the role cookie when the gate is configured. Driven against a production build: 401 anonymous, 200 with a redeemed judge cookie, 400 for spend=1 without an image, 409 when the budget is exhausted, 503 with no key - and the ledger file was never written.
closedGaps.costOfGettingThere: The obvious fix - deleting the NODE_ENV guard - would have opened a live YouCam harness to anyone holding a code, where one page refresh costs units. The route had to be split before it could be un-404'd.

closedGaps.title: Three render fixtures depicted three different people, served to whoever asked
closedGaps.how: Render fixtures are now keyed to the PERSON by content fingerprint, and try-on renders additionally to the garment id. apparel-gown.jpg, apparel-top.jpg and finish.jpg are deleted; the one genuine pair (samples/full-body.jpg in the Slate Blue suit) and the relight YouCam actually returned for samples/selfie.jpg (byte-identical to receipts/001) are all that remain. Every other combination refuses and the UI states that no captured render exists for this photo. tests/fixture-identity.test.ts pins the rule and fails if a fallback render returns.
closedGaps.costOfGettingThere: finish.jpg carried the whole look board as its editorial hero under alt text reading 'Your finished look, relit for the occasion', and it shipped that way into the 2026-08-10 Devpost screenshot gallery. Review 001 raised this defect class for uploads on 2026-08-09; the 2026-08-10 pass closed it for the skin mask only. Found by rendering the strip of sample and fixture images side by side and looking at it.

closedGaps.title: The fourth API rendered nothing a judge reached, and only one face ever produced a garment
closedGaps.how: Two approved tasks, both successful, both committed with their bytes: a Photo Lighting render of samples/full-body.jpg (receipts/002) and a cloth-v3 render putting the Sky Wrap Maxi Dress on samples/selfie-2.jpg (receipts/003). The wedding path now shows all four APIs with a receipt behind each render, and two faces visibly produce two different garments - the falsifiability the special category asks for. Both renders are keyed to the person they depict, so neither can leak onto another photo.
